To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a spatially located responsive reserve market is possible and is the best solution to the reserve market problem.
the locational reserve prices can be obtained from a co-optimization algorithm that minimizes the cost of the combined energy and reserves.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the spatial allocation of energy and reserves in the context of the locational marginal pricing (LMP) framework.
the development of a new method for allocating energy and reserve resources spatially, which will be useful for both transmission system planning and operation.
the development of a responsive-reserve market proposal that will be able to schedule reserves in a spatially optimal manner, and to price them according to their spatially located values.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
a responsive-reserve market is the best market structure to ensure grid reliability, while at the same time providing the least cost for both energy and reserves.
the proposed responsive reserve scheduling algorithm provides a practical and effective means for allocating and pricing energy and reserves in a way that is both spatially and temporally responsive.
a responsive reserve market is needed to address security issues and to ensure the reliability of the power system.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the proposed formulation can be used to schedule energy and reserves, and can also be used to price reserves in a locational sense.
the proposed formulation is capable of handling the spatially constrained energy and reserve markets and that it is likely to perform well in restructured markets.
we have developed a science-based method for allocating reserves and pricing them in a way that is responsive to the needs of the system.
The main takeaway from our work is that
reserves should be scheduled and priced in a similar way as energy, i.e., by using a locational pricing method.
a spatially located reserve market is necessary and that the locational marginal prices (LMPs) for reserves are not the same as the LMPs for power.
reserves are spatially located in the same manner that energy is, and that the locational reserve prices are also similar to the energy locational marginal prices.
